cohort: The study included 36 mother-neonate pairs with vaginal births and 42 mother-neonate pairs with caesarean sections.
finding: There was a high diversity of microbial communities in the pregnancy environment, and meconium microbial samples could be divided into three distinct types not influenced by the delivery method.
mod_finding: The distribution patterns of bacterial communities in the meconium, placenta, and foetal membranes were highly similar and had nothing to do with the mode of delivery.
cross-section timing: Samples (meconium, placenta, membrane, amniotic fluid for newborns; vaginal, rectal, oral for mothers) were collected around the time of birth.
